validity.recommendation: keep as a real proposed/cancelled international pipeline; correctly classified as gas; no duplicate on the 45-row roster
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE CONFIRMED independent of GEM/wiki, via sources gem.wiki itself cites (all re-verified live) plus one the wiki does not cite. Williams (NYSE: WMB) and Steelhead LNG Corp. jointly announced the Island Gas Connector Project on 2015-09-01 (Douglas Magazine, reprinting the joint release). Williams stood up a dedicated project site, islandgasconnector.com, which I read via Wayback (overview/benefits/timeline/regulatory pages, all captured 2017): an estimated 81-mile (129 km) natural gas pipeline, Sumas WA to Birch Bay/Custer WA (34 mi overland) then subsea across the Salish Sea (47 mi) to a landfall on Malahat Nation land near Mill Bay/Bamberton on Vancouver Island, BC, feeding Steelhead LNG's proposed Malahat LNG facility; Williams named as the party that 'would design, construct, operate and maintain' it; dual FERC (US)/NEB (Canada) jurisdiction, FERC pre-filing anticipated 2017, construction 'as early as summer 2019', in-service November 2020. Independent of Williams/Steelhead: Pipeline & Gas Journal's Pipeline News October-2018 'Planned Projects' PDF lists it (Operator, Length 80 mi, Diameter 36 in, Location Sumas WA-Vancouver Island BC, Completion 4Q2020, Status 'preparing to start the pre-filing process with FERC') -- an independent trade-press compilation, not a Williams/Steelhead page. Also independent: Water Is Life Movement, an anti-pipeline activist NGO (archived 2019-08/2019-10, unaffiliated with GEM/Williams/Steelhead though its text derives from operator materials), describes the same route/mileage split and opposition from the WSANEC/Saanich Inlet Network. islandgasconnector.com itself began 302-redirecting to Williams' corporate site (co.williams.com) from 2018-08-09 onward (Wayback CDX), i.e. the dedicated site was retired -- consistent with the project going dormant, though NOT itself a dated cancellation record (the PGJ trade pub still listed it as progressing toward FERC pre-filing in its October-2018 issue, published AFTER that redirect began). Classification (gas transmission, feeding an LNG export terminal) is correct. No other roster row describes this route -- not a duplicate. Gem.wiki's own prose is candid that its 'cancelled'-adjacent language is inferential: 'There have been no development updates since 2015 and the project is presumed to be cancelled' (its own infobox even reads Status: Proposed), which matches my finding that no source states a cancellation event -- see the spec concern below.

validity.recommendation: fix EndCountryOrArea from 'United States' to 'Canada' -- British Columbia (the sheet's own EndState/Province) is a Canadian province, not a US state
validity.researcher_notes: The worklist's Location [ref] unit carries an internal contradiction on the sheet: EndState/Province='British Columbia' but EndCountryOrArea='United States'. Every independent source (Williams' own project site, Water Is Life Movement, PGJ's Pipeline News listing, and gem.wiki's own prose 'a proposed natural gas pipeline in Washington, USA and British Columbia, Canada') agrees the pipeline runs from Sumas, Washington, USA to a landfall near Mill Bay/Bamberton on Vancouver Island, British Columbia, CANADA -- an international, cross-border line (hence dual FERC/NEB jurisdiction cited in every source). EndCountryOrArea='United States' is simply wrong and needs correcting to 'Canada'; corrected in the Location [ref] fill below.

validity.recommendation: treat ShelvedYear (2017) and CancelledYear (2019) as unconfirmed placeholders, not sourced facts -- no document states either date, and the recorded years are contradicted by, and internally inconsistent with, the evidence
validity.researcher_notes: Two independent problems. (1) Evidence contradiction: ShelvedYear=2017 implies the project had already gone dormant by 2017, but the independent Pipeline & Gas Journal trade listing, published October 2018, still describes it as an ACTIVE proposal 'preparing to start the pre-filing process with FERC' with a targeted 4Q2020 completion -- i.e. still being pursued more than a year after the sheet's claimed shelving. Williams' own project site was also still live and unchanged (per Wayback) through at least September 2017, and only began redirecting to Williams' corporate site from 2018-08-09 -- itself not a dated cancellation notice, just a site retirement, and even that postdates 2017. So 2017 cannot be right as a 'no more progress' cutoff. (2) Internal inconsistency: this batch's own dormancy convention is '2y no progress -> shelved; shelved +4y -> cancelled'. Proposed 2015 + 2y = 2017 shelved is at least formula-consistent, but shelved 2017 + 4y = 2021, not the sheet's CancelledYear=2019 -- the two recorded years don't satisfy the sheet's own inference rule, suggesting they were entered without applying it consistently (or without dated evidence at all). I could not find ANY document -- FERC docket, NEB/CER filing, company statement, or press -- that states a specific shelving or cancellation date; the islandgasconnector.com redirect (Aug 2018) is the only dated signal of inactivity I found, and it only sets a floor (project was not yet abandoned as of the PGJ Oct-2018 listing) not a firm shelved/cancelled year. Recommend leaving ShelvedCancelledType='inferred' (not 'confirmed' -- no dated, sourced cancellation exists) and treating both year fields as needing revision rather than pasting them forward as fact. Both Shelved [ref] and Cancelled [ref] fills below are UNRESOLVED for the same reason.

validity.recommendation: do not fill Operator until the conflict is resolved -- Williams' own materials vs. the PGJ trade listing disagree on who would operate the line
validity.researcher_notes: Two sources genuinely disagree. Williams' own regulatory page (islandgasconnector.com, via Wayback) states in as many words: 'Williams would design, construct, operate and maintain the proposed Island Gas Connector Project.' The overview page adds that Williams is 'the owner and operator of Northwest Pipeline' -- naming Williams, not Northwest Pipeline itself, as the party building/operating THIS new line. But the independent Pipeline & Gas Journal Pipeline News (Oct 2018) 'Planned Projects' listing names 'Operator: Steelhead LNG Corp.' for the Island Gas Connector project. These cannot both be literally true; PGJ's project database may simply have logged the LNG sponsor (Steelhead) as the public face of the project rather than the pipeline company, but I have no way to confirm that reading. Leaving Operator UNRESOLVED (see fill below) rather than guessing between the two.

fills.researcher_notes: No document states 'cancelled' (or an equivalent withdrawal/termination) for this project. The nearest dated evidence -- PGJ's Pipeline News, Oct 2018 -- describes it as still 'preparing to start the pre-filing process with FERC', i.e. still alive at that point. Gem.wiki's own prose calls the cancellation a presumption from silence, not a sourced fact ('There have been no development updates since 2015 and the project is presumed to be cancelled'). Given a decade of total inactivity (no FERC pre-filing docket, no NEB/CER filing, dedicated project site retired since 2018, Steelhead LNG itself has shown no public activity in years) 'cancelled' remains the most reasonable practical characterization, but I have no ref that literally supports it -- see the spec concern in validity[] for the same reasoning applied to the year fields. Searched: elibrary.ferc.gov (no PF-docket found under Williams/Northwest Pipeline for this project), general web search (WebSearch budget was exhausted mid-session; DuckDuckGo/Bing/Ecosia/Mojeek all returned JS-gated/challenge pages to curl).

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Newest dated evidence found is the PGJ Pipeline News October-2018 listing, which still shows the project pre-regulatory ('preparing to start the pre-filing process with FERC') rather than shelved. After that, nothing: islandgasconnector.com began redirecting to Williams' corporate site from 2018-08-09 onward and never came back (checked Wayback CDX through 2023); no FERC pre-filing docket was ever opened (none found searching elibrary.ferc.gov for Williams/Northwest Pipeline + 'Island Gas Connector'); no NEB/CER project page; no press beyond 2015-2019 activist/trade mentions; Steelhead LNG itself shows no signs of ongoing activity in recent years. Applying this batch's own dormancy convention loosely (proposed 2015, no confirmed progress past a 2018 pre-filing announcement, now 2026) easily clears both the 2-year and 4-year thresholds for 'cancelled' in practice, so I am NOT recommending a change away from cancelled. What I AM flagging (see validity[] spec concern) is that the sheet's specific ShelvedYear=2017 and CancelledYear=2019 are not supported by any dated document and are contradicted by the Oct-2018 evidence that the project was still moving forward -- so 'confirm' here means 'cancelled/dormant is the right characterization', not 'the recorded years are right'. ShelvedCancelledType should stay 'inferred': I found no FERC order, NEB filing, company statement, or press report of an actual cancellation/withdrawal, only an absence of further activity.

summary: Real, correctly-classified cross-border proposal (Williams + Steelhead LNG, Sumas WA -> Malahat LNG on Vancouver Island BC), confirmed via PGJ trade press + an independent NGO page + Williams' own retired project site -- not a GEM-only phantom, not a duplicate; length/diameter/start-year/owner/fuel now sourced (REFS_ADDED), but EndCountryOrArea was wrong (fixed United States -> Canada), and ShelvedYear=2017/CancelledYear=2019/Operator are all unconfirmed (UNRESOLVED) -- no dated cancellation evidence exists and the years are internally inconsistent with the sheet's own dormancy rule.
